title: Video Streaming Platform (Netflix / OTT): Complete Architecture
description: Design a global video-on-demand (VOD) streaming service (Netflix scale) with Open Connect CDN, per-title encoding, DRM licensing, and adaptive bitrate delivery.

data.text: Design a global Video-on-Demand (VOD) streaming platform like Netflix or Disney+ serving 250+ million subscribers streaming over 100 million hours of premium video daily. The system must ingest high-resolution studio master files (ProRes), execute distributed per-title and per-shot encoding into hundreds of video/audio/subtitle permutations, enforce multi-DRM content protection (Widevine, FairPlay, PlayReady), and stream 4K HDR streams with sub-second startup using custom edge appliances (Open Connect) embedded directly within Internet Service Provider (ISP) networks.

terms.definition: Custom hardware caching servers deployed by Netflix directly inside ISP networks and internet exchange points (IXPs), serving 95%+ of video traffic locally.
Dynamically tailoring compression bitrates based on visual complexity (e.g. an animated cartoon needs 1.5 Mbps for 1080p, while an action movie requires 6 Mbps).
Encrypting video segments with Common Encryption (CENC) and exchanging decryption keys via platform-specific DRM license servers (Apple FairPlay, Google Widevine, Microsoft PlayReady).
Segmenting video into 2-6 second chunks; client media players monitor buffer health and download speed to switch bitrate levels without rebuffering.
The uncompressed, pristine studio master file (often 500GB+ per movie) used as the source for all downstream transcoding profiles.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Studio Ingestion & Quality Control: Ingest massive master files, validate color spaces, audio channels, and subtitles
Distributed Transcoding Pipeline: Encode videos across AV1, HEVC, and H.264 codecs at resolutions from 360p up to 4K HDR
Adaptive Bitrate Playback: Stream audio and video seamlessly adapting to fluctuating cellular and Wi-Fi speeds
Multi-DRM Content Protection: Enforce license verification, device revocation, and hardware-backed decryption
Watch Progress Synchronization: Save playback position (to the second) to enable instant cross-device resume
Personalized Content Hub: Curate personalized movie carousels, genre recommendations, and localized artwork

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Scale: 250M+ paying subscribers; 100M+ concurrent hours streamed daily; Terabits/sec peak egress
Playback Startup Latency: <1 second time-to-first-frame from pressing Play to video playback
Rebuffering Ratio: Under 0.25% of total watch time spent rebuffering or stalled
DRM Security: Zero tolerance for key leaks; full hardware DRM support on Smart TVs and mobile chipsets
Availability: 99.999% uptime for the playback authorization and license delivery cluster

data.text: Netflix separates control plane operations (User Auth, Recommendations, Billing, DRM Licensing) hosted in AWS Cloud from the massive data delivery plane (Video Bit Streaming) handled by ISP-embedded Open Connect Appliances (OCAs).

data.text: When a user presses Play, the client validates account rights, resolves the nearest ISP-embedded caching appliance (OCA), retrieves the hardware DRM decryption key, and begins streaming chunks.

faqs.question: Why did Netflix build Open Connect instead of relying exclusively on commercial CDNs (Akamai/CloudFront)?
faqs.answer: Commercial CDNs charge per gigabyte delivered. At Netflix scale (tens of petabytes every hour), commercial CDN transit fees would run into billions of dollars annually. By manufacturing custom appliances (OCAs) loaded with hundreds of terabytes of NVMe/HDDs and installing them for free inside ISP data centers, traffic never leaves the ISP's internal network. This saves transit costs for both Netflix and the ISP while guaranteeing sub-10ms delivery latency.

faqs.question: What is Per-Shot Encoding and why does it revolutionize bandwidth efficiency?
faqs.answer: Traditional encoders apply uniform compression settings across an entire 2-hour movie. But a static conversation in a cafe requires very few bits, whereas an explosion scene in a superhero movie requires massive bitrate to avoid pixelation. Per-shot encoding breaks a film into individual camera cuts (shots) and calculates the optimal rate-distortion curve (using VMAF metric) for each shot, slashing bandwidth consumption by 30-40% without sacrificing perceptual quality.

faqs.question: How is watch progress synchronized across multiple devices without database lag?
faqs.answer: Every 5-10 seconds of active playback, the client emits a lightweight UDP/HTTP heartbeat containing `{profile_id, movie_id, timestamp_seconds}`. A stateless ingestion layer writes this to a write-back Redis cache and Kafka. If a viewer turns off their TV and opens their tablet, the tablet reads the bookmark directly from Redis in <5ms, resuming playback at the exact second.

faqs.question: How are new TV shows distributed to thousands of OCAs before a midnight premiere?
faqs.answer: New releases are never pulled on-demand during premiere hour (which would cause a cache stampede). Instead, during off-peak night hours (2:00 AM - 5:00 AM), Netflix's proactive replication engine pre-positions and copies new episodes from AWS S3 to every OCA worldwide via peer-to-peer and unicast distribution. When users click Play at midnight, the video is already sitting on local ISP disks.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Decoupled architecture: AWS cloud handles metadata and licensing; ISP-embedded OCAs deliver raw video
Per-shot encoding dynamically optimizes bitrate per camera cut, saving 30%+ network bandwidth
Multi-DRM integration (Widevine, FairPlay, PlayReady) pairs with Common Encryption for premium 4K security
Pre-positioning off-peak replication ensures blockbuster premieres never trigger origin cache stampedes
Sub-second watch bookmarks synchronize across devices via fast in-memory Redis caches
data.takeaway: Global OTT streaming platforms scale by pushing media bits directly into local ISP networks through dedicated caching appliances, using advanced per-shot compression and cloud orchestration to deliver pristine 4K video.
